text:
Utah might be the most frustrating team in the West to watch right now. The Mammoth control games: 57% of the five-on-five expected goals, the measure of who gets the better chances, one of the best marks in the league. And yet they are winless in three and 1-3-1 in their last five, outscored 22-15. The easy culprit is in net. Karel Vejmelka is at .866 and 7.2 goals saved below expected this season, .847 over his last five starts. A team this good at driving play should not be scrambling for points in November, and the gap between their chances and their results is the story of their season so far.

It gets harder tonight. Utah lost 5-3 in Las Vegas last night and is on the second half of a back-to-back, and two of its best young forwards are out: Logan Cooley (upper body), who has 21 points in 18 games and has been the most written-about player on the team, and Dylan Guenther, on injured reserve until early December. Clayton Keller has moved beside Vincent Trocheck and Lawson Crouse; Keller has ten points in a six-game streak and Trocheck is one assist from 400 for his career. Kailer Yamamoto and Daniil But are getting bigger minutes.

St. Louis snapped a three-game winless run on Tuesday against Detroit, with Pius Suter reaching both 100 career goals and 200 points in the same night. The Blues are a 50-50 team at five on five, and Joel Hofer has been their steadiest piece: .921, 6.7 goals saved above expected. His partner Jordan Binnington has spent the week in trade rumors. Logan Mailloux made his season debut Tuesday. Dylan Holloway has no goals in eight games on 3.4 expected goals.

Our Sleeper is Philip Broberg, projected for 26 minutes tonight, up from 24:36 on the season; we have him at 49% for a point. Our numbers have Utah at 3.17 expected goals and St. Louis at 2.98.
headline: Utah's best process, worst goaltending
